_note: Titles and descriptions for the examples gallery (ROADMAP Task 314). Keyed by file name. Everything else in the manifest is DERIVED from the project itself by dev/scripts/generate_examples.php -- node and link counts, unit system, thumbnail -- so this file holds only what a machine cannot work out. A description is what makes a wall of titles browsable; it should say what the network IS and what it is good for looking at, not restate the counts sitting beside it. Keep them to one line: they are card subtitles, not documentation.

Basic-example-SI-units-lpn.json.title: Basic network, SI units
Basic-example-SI-units-lpn.json.description: Start here. A reservoir, a pump and a small loop: the least a working water network can be. Metres, millimetres and litres per second.

Basic-example-US-units-lpn.json.title: Basic network, US units
Basic-example-US-units-lpn.json.description: The same starting network in feet, inches and gallons per minute.

Net1-lpn.json.title: EPANET Net1
Net1-lpn.json.description: The smallest of EPANET's own three sample networks: one reservoir, a pump and a single loop. US units (gpm).

Net2-lpn.json.title: EPANET Net2
Net2-lpn.json.description: A branched distribution system with a tank, from EPANET's samples. US units (gpm).

Net3-lpn.json.title: EPANET Net3
Net3-lpn.json.description: EPANET's large sample: 97 junctions, two tanks and a river source. Worth opening to see how a real-sized model reads. US units (gpm).

Elm-Street-Center-lpn.json.title: Elm Street Center
Elm-Street-Center-lpn.json.description: A commercial site's fire-flow-plus-max-day design snapshot, drawn over a CAD site plan. US units (gpm).
